newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-PATRIOTS AGREE TO THREE-YEAR EXTENSION WITH TE BEN COATES.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-PATRIOTS AGREE TO THREE-YEAR EXTENSION WITH TE BEN COATES.

text.p: Three-time Pro Bowl tight end Ben Coates, the favourite target of quarterback Drew Bledsoe, will remain with the New England Patriots through the year 2000 after agreeing to a three-year contract extension Friday.
The 28-year-old Coates caught 62 passes for 682 yards and a career-high nine touchdowns last season in helping the Patriots reach the Super Bowl.
In six seasons, Coates has started 60 of 96 games and totalled 325 receptions for 3,696 yards and 34 touchdowns.
"Ben Coates is the premier tight end in the league today and is a vital part of our offence," said Patriots owner Robert Kraft in announcing the new contract.

"Two years ago, we made a long-term commitment to quarterback Drew Bledsoe. Since then, we have made long-term commitments to wide receivers Terry Glenn, Shawn Jefferson, Vincent Brisby and now tight end Ben Coates in an effort to maintain one of the top offensive arsenals in the league into the next millenium."

A 1991 fifth-round draft pick, Coates emerged as a starter in 1993 and led the team with 53 catches for 659 yards and eight touchdowns. He followed that season by setting an NFL reception record for tight ends and a club single-season reception record of 96 for 1,174 yards and seven scores.
Coates again led the Patriots in catches in 1995 with 84 for 915 yards and six touchdowns. His 325 career receptions rank third on the team's all-time list.
